Many carriers object to application of the proposed population-mileage formula to New York City. They argue that a 20 mile radius creates a zone which is too broad, and that the zone will be difficult to define because the corporate limits of New York City are extended by harbor islands and are difficult to ascertain. They argue further that Staten Island, although it is a part of the city, should not be used in applying the formula since it is essentially suburban in nature. These carriers contend that New York City is unique in that surrounding communities are in competition with, rather that economically a part of the city. They also point out that New York City is comprised of five counties, each of which is a separate community, and they suggest that it be treated like a consolidated government with its commercial zone confined to its corporate limits. These motor carriers also object to the proposed sections 1048.11 and 1048.12 which partially remove the exemption from communities in New Jersey, and in Westchester and Nassau Counties, N.Y., which are within the proposed expanded zone. They assert that there is no justification for treating these communities differently from all others, and that the partial removal of the exemption will favor unregulated carriers.
